title: Goroutine leak on panic in executeStructured
body: The startStructuredOutputCapture function starts a goroutine that runs indefinitely until cancelled. In executeStructured (line 114), the cleanup function is called immediately after app.Harness returns, but there is no defer statement. If app.Harness panics, the cleanup function is never called, causing the goroutine to leak indefinitely. The goroutine will continue looping, calling filepath.Glob every 20ms and consuming CPU resources.
evidence:
Step 1: executeStructured calls startStructuredOutputCapture at line 114, which starts a goroutine that loops until cancelled
Step 2: The goroutine executes `for { scan(); select { case <-watchCtx.Done(): return; case <-ticker.C: } }` indefinitely
Step 3: If app.Harness(ctx, prompt, schema, &dest, opts) at line 115 panics, the function stack unwinds
Step 4: The cleanup function stopOutputCapture() at line 116 is never called due to the panic
Step 5: The goroutine continues running indefinitely, calling filepath.Glob every 20ms without cleanup

title: seedDefaults masks diagnostic information about system failures
dimension_name: seedDefaults error masking potential diagnostic issues
body: The seedDefaults fallback at lines 150-152 silently converts potential diagnostic information into a default-seeded value, hiding critical system issues. When result == nil (indicating a fundamental API/auth/provider failure) or result.Parsed == nil due to unexpected errors, the code returns a default value with nil error instead of propagating the diagnostic information. This violates the error handling principle that billing/auth/provider failures should not be hidden behind default values.
evidence:
Step 1: app.Harness returns result, err where result could be nil due to API failures
Step 2: fatal.CheckFatalHarnessError already filters out some fatal errors at line 137
Step 3: But if result is nil due to non-fatal but diagnostic-worthy errors, line 150 triggers seedDefaults
Step 4: Line 151 returns &seeded, result, nil - masking the fact that result was nil and hiding potentially important diagnostic information
Step 5: Callers like Run cannot distinguish between successful execution and system failures that were masked by defaults
